pages.text: "Give me that pot! Now!" Impatient Bobo ran to the play-house area. Timid Lala was putting acorns in a pot. "I have not finished yet..."
Bobo wanted to make acorn soup in the pot, but Lala still held it. "I want to do it now too!" Bobo stamped their feet.
Bobo pushed the pot out of Lala's hands and snatched it. Acorns scattered across the floor. Lala curled both hands and stepped back.
Bobo was alone in the play area. Stirring an empty pot was no fun. "Lala..." Bobo called, but Lala remained turned away.
Teacher Bau of Rainbow Class sat in the play area. "Bobo, your hands went first. Use words, not shoves!" Teacher Bau picked up an acorn and placed it in Bobo's hand.
Bobo pulled the purple hat brim forward. Their heart thumped and face burned. "I... pushed." Bobo took one step toward Lala.
"Lala, I am sorry. I wanted to make soup too. Let us do it together." Lala turned and offered the pot. Bobo took it in both hands. "Thank you!"
They picked up acorns and dropped them into the pot. Bobo stirred; Lala served it on plates. Much more fun than stirring alone.
The next day, Lala held the ladle first. Bobo clasped both hands behind their back. "One, hands behind! Two, ask with words! Three, decide turns! Lala, give me a turn when you finish!"
Teacher Bau hugged one with each arm. Pushing kept everyone from playing; words let two play. Taking Lala's offered ladle, Bobo called, "Use words, not shoves!"
